source.title: Dynamic of Stochastic Gradient Descent with State-Dependent Noise
source.authors: Qi Meng; Shiqi Gong; Wei Chen; Zhi-Ming Ma; Tie-Yan Liu

record.file_problem: none noted; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies minibatch size and reports test accuracy after training to convergence, bearing on the batch-size/generalization version. It also measures a parameter-distribution statistic associated with test accuracy, but does not measure the magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper reports six batch-size test-accuracy results for LeNet-5 and ResNet-18 and says that larger κ accompanies lower LeNet-5 test accuracy. The parameter-distribution fits and κ values are reported as experimental findings; the broader architecture and pretrained-model results are not mapped to a version here.
record.test_reason: The study varies minibatch size and measures held-out accuracy, bearing on V5. LeNet-5 is trained to convergence; Appendix 7.5.2 gives ResNet-18 a shared epoch-based decay schedule and describes convergence after 250 epochs. The record overlooks this scheduling information. Neither κ nor the theoretical Hessian-based bounds measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors argue that state-dependent gradient noise helps SGD escape sharp minima and implicitly favors models with better generalization. Their empirical evidence includes power-law fits, increasing κ with batch size, declining LeNet-5 accuracy with κ, and synthetic escape experiments. The generalization mechanism is a theoretical interpretation; the reported ResNet-18 accuracies do not decline monotonically with κ.
record.recipe_differences: The study models SGD using a proposed state-dependent power-law diffusion, derives escape-time and PAC-Bayes results, and compares model parameter distributions and simulated escape behavior. It does not reproduce the claim versions' original experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Minibatch size changes estimated κ and reported test accuracy; batch-size effects differ between LeNet-5 and ResNet-18.

fits_no_version.finding: LeNet-5 accuracy decreases as fitted κ increases, with all training losses below 0.001. ResNet-18 accuracy is not monotonic in κ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fitted weight-distribution κ tracks generalization in the reported LeNet-5 runs, with model-dependent applicability.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected layer-weight distributions are fitted by power-law κ distributions, and κ increases with batch size in the controlled network experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selected SGD-trained layer-weight distributions admit power-law fits whose fitted tail parameter depends on batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: The study derives escape-time and PAC-Bayes bounds using Hessian-based flatness and tests escape behavior in a synthetic two-dimensional landscape.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the study's assumptions, state-dependent diffusion can accelerate escape from sharp basins and yield bounds associated with flatness.

record.problems: The minibatch comparison is reported after training until convergence, without a fixed-epoch comparison. The displayed results provide no uncertainty estimates. The claimed κ–generalization relation is described for LeNet-5; the reported ResNet-18 test accuracies do not follow a monotonic decline as κ increases.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible findings omitted. Results on covariance curves and the simulated 2-D escape success rates do not measure a version's stated generalization behavior.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy under matching recipes.
Width increases beyond interpolation and their effects on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and interventions on local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning or optimizer switching.

A clearly fixed common epoch budget for LeNet-5; an unambiguous identical stopping epoch for ResNet-18; controlled tests of longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization, or regularization adaptations; language models.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, measured training–test gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 3 confirms all extracted accuracy and κ values. Appendix 7.5.2 supplies material ResNet-18 recipe and epoch information omitted from the record. No supplied claim version is an original contribution of this study, so original-source exclusion does not apply.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep past interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under tuning.
The stated fixed-epoch comparison and recipe adaptations such as longer training, warmup, normalization, or regularization changes.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation sharpness and comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: LeNet-5 on MNIST, batch 1024 versus 64, trained to convergence
relationships.reason: R1 and R3 show accuracy falling from 98.89% to 91.17% despite training losses below 0.001. This supports the large-batch penalty component; it does not establish the fixed-epoch condition.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy was lower despite very low training losses at convergence, but the comparison and equal epoch budgets remain unverified.

relationships.condition: LeNet-5 on MNIST, batch 256 versus 64, trained to convergence
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 show only a 0.08-point accuracy reduction, with no uncertainty reported; the penalty is much smaller than at batch 1024.
relationships.display_finding: A 0.08-percentage-point accuracy reduction was reported without uncertainty, but the batch comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, batch 256 versus 64, with the Appendix 7.5.2 recipe
relationships.reason: R4 and R5 show accuracy improving from 94.87% to 95.36%, so increasing batch size does not uniformly hurt here. This does not establish a contradiction beyond the workload-dependent threshold.
relationships.display_finding: An accuracy improvement from 94.87% to 95.36% was reported, but this comparison remains unverified. It does not identify a batch size above which accuracy falls.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, batch 1024 versus 64, with the Appendix 7.5.2 recipe
relationships.reason: R4 and R6 show accuracy falling from 94.87% to 94.26%. The appendix specifies common decay milestones and convergence after 250 epochs, but does not unequivocally establish identical stopping epochs.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy was lower with the larger batch, but the comparison and identical stopping epochs remain unverified.
